skill.title: Find the present value of a series of payments (pension/annuity)
needs: Find the present value of a future sum
Sum n terms of a geometric series

steps.title: Set up the present value of each payment

lines.text: The first payment of $\text{€}20\,000$ is paid on the day of retirement. Then 25 more payments follow, each $1\%$ larger. Each is discounted by $1.024$ per year.
The terms inside the bracket form a GP. There are 26 terms, from power 0 to power 25.

steps.title: Find the present value of each remaining repayment

lines.text: Each repayment is divided by $1.003$ once for every month from now until it is paid.
The first remaining repayment is 1 month away, the last is 168 months away.
First term $a = \dfrac{1771}{1.003}$, common ratio $r = \dfrac{1}{1.003}$, and $n = 168$ terms.

skill.title: Derive the mortgage repayment formula
skill.input: loan = sum of PVs of repayments
skill.example: P = A/(1 + i) + … + A/(1 + i)ᵗ ⇒ formula
needs: Find the repayment on a loan/mortgage
Sum n terms of a geometric series

steps.title: Write the loan as the sum of the repayments in today's money

lines.text: A repayment $A$ made at the end of period $k$ is worth $\frac{A}{(1+i)^k}$ today. Today's value of all $t$ repayments is the loan $P$.

steps.title: Use the sum of a geometric series

lines.text: This is a geometric series with first term $a = \frac{A}{1+i}$, common ratio $r = \frac{1}{1+i}$ and $t$ terms, so $S_t = \frac{a(1 - r^t)}{1 - r}$.

steps.title: Cancel the factor 1/(1+i) and tidy up

lines.text: Multiply both sides by $i(1+i)^t$, then divide both sides by $(1+i)^t - 1$.

steps.title: Write the monthly rate as a decimal

lines.text: Each month the debt grows by a factor of $1 + 0.00279 = 1.00279$.
A payment made after $n$ months is divided by $1.00279$ once for each month.

steps.title: Set up the amount borrowed as a sum

lines.text: The loan equals the sum of the present values of all $25 \times 12 = 300$ repayments.
This is a geometric series with $n = 300$, first term $a$ and common ratio $r$.
